articles.title: Kenya hosts Africa's China-backed university innovation competition
articles.titleCn: 肯尼亚举办非洲第二届中国高校创新创业大赛
articles.summary: First launched in China, the event expanded overseas in 2025, with Kenya becoming the first country outside China to host the African regional competition. Following the inaugural African edition last year, Kenya once again staged the event this year.
articles.summaryCn: 肯尼亚主办了第二届中国国际大学生创新大赛非洲赛区，汇聚非洲青年创新者展示解决粮食安全、医疗等挑战的方案，并促进中非教育科技合作。

paragraphs.en: Kenya hosted the second African edition of the China International College Students' Innovation Competition, bringing together young innovators from across the continent to {{0}} practical {{1}} to challenges including food security, healthcare, biotechnology and sustainable agriculture. The competition is organized by the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China together with 11 other institutions. First launched in China, the event {{2}} overseas in 2025, with Kenya becoming the first country outside China to host the African {{3}} competition. Following the {{4}} African edition last year, Kenya once again staged the event this year. The competition encourages university students to translate classroom learning into innovative solutions for real-world problems while {{5}} educational and scientific cooperation between Africa and China.
paragraphs.cn: 肯尼亚主办了第二届中国国际大学生创新大赛非洲赛区，汇聚了来自非洲大陆各地的青年创新者，展示应对粮食安全、医疗保健、生物技术和可持续农业等挑战的实用解决方案。该大赛由中华人民共和国教育部及其他11家机构共同组织。该赛事最初在中国启动，于2025年扩展到海外，肯尼亚成为首个在中国以外举办非洲区域赛的国家。继去年首届非洲赛区后，肯尼亚今年再次承办。大赛鼓励大学生将课堂所学转化为解决实际问题的创新方案，同时加强非洲与中国之间的教育和科学合作。

paragraphs.en:
Students from various universties from Africa receive gold and silver medals during the China International College Students' Innovation Competition in Nairobi, Kenya, July 28, 2026. Africa
Kenyan education officials said supporting young innovators is {{6}} given Africa's youthful population. "I think one of the most important things for us is really to look at ways and means of how we can be able to support our youth," a Kenyan education official said. "In Kenya, 75% of the population is aged 35 and below, while Africa has almost 400 million young people in the same age bracket. We want to {{7}} their creativity and provide {{8}} by helping them develop their talents," said Professor Shaukat Abdulrazak, Kenya's Principal Secretary for the State Department for Science, Research and Innovation.
paragraphs.cn: 来自非洲各大学的学生在2026年7月28日于肯尼亚内罗毕举行的中国国际大学生创新大赛中获得金银奖。肯尼亚教育官员表示，鉴于非洲青年人口众多，支持青年创新者至关重要。一位肯尼亚教育官员说：“我认为对我们来说最重要的事情之一，就是真正寻找支持青年的方式和方法。”肯尼亚科学、研究与创新部首席秘书Shaukat Abdulrazak教授表示：“肯尼亚75%的人口年龄在35岁及以下，而非洲有近4亿年轻人处于同一年龄段。我们希望培养他们的创造力，通过指导帮助他们发展才能。”

paragraphs.en:
Professor Abdulrazak said the {{9}} {{10}} between Africa and China, and between Kenya and China since independence, continues to create opportunities for cooperation in education, innovation and skills development. Nanjing Agricultural University Vice President, Professor Feng Shuyi said the competition pushes students beyond academic theory by requiring them to develop practical solutions to {{11}} challenges. "The competition encourages university students to apply what they have learned in the classroom to real-world problems," Feng said. Professor Feng Shuyi, Vice President of Nanjing Agricultural University, during the China International College Students' Innovation Competition in Nairobi, Kenya, July 28, 2026. Africa
Many of the projects presented focused on improving food security, tackling water {{12}}, preventing crop diseases and advancing healthcare technologies.
paragraphs.cn: Abdulrazak教授表示，非洲与中国之间，以及肯尼亚与中国自独立以来的长期伙伴关系，继续为教育、创新和技能发展领域的合作创造机会。南京农业大学副校长冯淑怡教授表示，大赛通过要求学生开发解决社会挑战的实用方案，推动学生超越学术理论。冯淑怡说：“大赛鼓励大学生将课堂所学应用于现实问题。”2026年7月28日，南京农业大学副校长冯淑怡教授在肯尼亚内罗毕举行的中国国际大学生创新大赛上发言。许多展示的项目侧重于改善粮食安全、解决水资源短缺、预防作物病害和推进医疗技术。

paragraphs.en: Professor Abdulrazak said that the competition gives students an opportunity to use innovation and technology to solve problems affecting communities. "I was very {{14}} to see some of the projects related to health, including traditional Chinese medicine that is being {{15}} by the African younger generation. We also saw areas of biotechnology aimed at {{13}} food safety and food security," Prof. Abdulrazak said. Professor Shaukat Abdulrazak, Kenya's Principal Secretary for the State Department for Science, Research and Innovation, during the China International College Students' Innovation Competition in Nairobi, Kenya, July 28, 2026.
paragraphs.cn: Abdulrazak教授表示，大赛为学生提供了利用创新和技术解决影响社区问题的机会。Abdulrazak教授说：“我印象深刻的是，一些与健康相关的项目，包括非洲年轻一代正在实施的中医药项目。我们还看到了旨在增强食品安全和粮食安全的生物技术领域。”2026年7月28日，肯尼亚科学、研究与创新部首席秘书Shaukat Abdulrazak教授在肯尼亚内罗毕举行的中国国际大学生创新大赛上发言。

paragraphs.en:
Africa
Among the gold medal-winning projects was one from Malawi's Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources, which showcased an innovation designed to improve agricultural {{16}} for smallholder farmers. Ufulu Kampinga, a student at the university, said the project, titled Malawi Youth Hope Seeds in Africa Science and Technology Backyard Entrepreneurship Project, aims to improve farmers' incomes, {{17}} and crop production. "Our project is helping smallholder farmers in Malawi earn more, eat enough and eat better," Kampinga said. "We encourage practices such as {{18}} maize with soybeans to improve nutrition while increasing harvests so farmers can strengthen their food security throughout the year."
Fellow student Monica Didas said the team developed the project to address {{19}} farming challenges. "Using this technology and the model introduced through China's support, we have been able to overcome some of those challenges," Didas said.
paragraphs.cn: 在获得金奖的项目中，有一个来自马拉维利隆圭农业与自然资源大学，展示了一项旨在提高小农户农业生产力的创新。该大学学生Ufulu Kampinga表示，这个名为“马拉维青年希望种子非洲科技小院创业项目”的项目旨在提高农民的收入、营养和作物产量。Kampinga说：“我们的项目正在帮助马拉维的小农户赚更多钱、吃饱吃好。”他补充道：“我们鼓励玉米与大豆间作等做法，以改善营养，同时提高收成，使农民全年加强粮食安全。”同学Monica Didas表示，团队开发该项目是为了应对持续的农业挑战。Didas说：“通过这项技术和中国支持引入的模式，我们得以克服其中一些挑战。”

paragraphs.en:
The competition also highlighted {{20}} in healthcare and traditional medicine. Hu Zijing, an associate professor at the University of Johannesburg who teaches traditional Chinese medicine, said the initiative strengthens exchanges between African and Chinese students. "This platform enhances {{21}} understanding and collaboration between young people from Africa and China," Hu said. "It enables students to showcase their work, better understand one another and develop an international outlook."
He added that the goal extends beyond introducing traditional Chinese medicine in Africa. "We want to {{22}} Chinese medicine with African traditional medicine because Africa also has a very long history of traditional medicine," he said.
paragraphs.cn: 大赛还突出了医疗保健和传统医学领域的合作。约翰内斯堡大学副教授、教授中医药的Hu Zijing表示，该倡议加强了非洲和中国学生之间的交流。Hu说：“这个平台增进了非洲和中国年轻人之间的相互理解和合作。它使学生能够展示他们的工作，更好地相互了解，并培养国际视野。”他补充说，目标不仅仅是把中医药引入非洲。他说：“我们希望将中医与非洲传统医学相结合，因为非洲也有非常悠久的传统医学历史。”

paragraphs.en:
University of Johannesburg student Rabone Monama demonstrated a traditional Chinese medicine {{23}} model used to help patients with arthritis, dysmenorrhea and other pain-related conditions. Monama said studying traditional Chinese medicine had taught her that healthcare extends beyond medication. "We learn from nature how we live, how we eat and how we manage our emotions," she said. "The food we eat is also medicine. We can learn to take care of ourselves through healthy lifestyles before medical {{24}} becomes necessary."
Elina Hlatshwayo, a student at Johannesburg University where she's studying traditional Chinese medicine, during the China International College Students' Innovation Competition in Nairobi, Kenya, July 28, 2026.
paragraphs.cn: 约翰内斯堡大学学生Rabone Monama展示了一种中医药康复模型，用于帮助关节炎、痛经和其他疼痛相关疾病患者。Monama表示，学习中医药让她明白，医疗保健不仅仅是药物。她说：“我们从自然中学习如何生活、如何饮食、如何管理情绪。我们吃的食物也是药物。我们可以在需要医疗干预之前，通过健康的生活方式学会照顾自己。”2026年7月28日，约翰内斯堡大学学生Elina Hlatshwayo在肯尼亚内罗毕举行的中国国际大学生创新大赛上发言。

paragraphs.en:
Africa
Fellow student Elina Hlatshwayo said participating in the competition helped her develop skills beyond her academic training. "Our course is heavily focused on clinical studies and traditional Chinese medicine, so this project allowed me to explore the technical aspects, including physics and chemistry," Hlatshwayo said. Other participating institutions included Kenya's Egerton University and Kabarak University, alongside Uganda's Makerere University. Organizers say the competition continues to provide a platform for African and Chinese university students to collaborate, exchange ideas and develop innovations capable of addressing shared development challenges while preparing the next generation of innovators and {{25}}.
paragraphs.cn: 同学Elina Hlatshwayo表示，参加大赛帮助她培养了超出学术训练的技能。Hlatshwayo说：“我们的课程主要侧重于临床研究和中医药，所以这个项目让我探索了技术方面，包括物理和化学。”其他参与机构包括肯尼亚的埃格顿大学和卡巴拉克大学，以及乌干达的马克雷雷大学。组织者表示，大赛继续为非洲和中国大学生提供平台，以合作、交流思想并开发能够应对共同发展挑战的创新，同时培养下一代创新者和企业家。

articles.fullText:
Kenya hosted the second African edition of the China International College Students' Innovation Competition, bringing together young innovators from across the continent to showcase practical solutions to challenges including food security, healthcare, biotechnology and sustainable agriculture.
The competition is organized by the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China together with 11 other institutions.
First launched in China, the event expanded overseas in 2025, with Kenya becoming the first country outside China to host the African regional competition. Following the inaugural African edition last year, Kenya once again staged the event this year.
The competition encourages university students to translate classroom learning into innovative solutions for real-world problems while strengthening educational and scientific cooperation between Africa and China.
Students from various universties from Africa receive gold and silver medals during the China International College Students' Innovation Competition in Nairobi, Kenya, July 28, 2026. 
 Africa
Kenyan education officials said supporting young innovators is crucial given Africa's youthful population.
"I think one of the most important things for us is really to look at ways and means of how we can be able to support our youth," a Kenyan education official said. "In Kenya, 75% of the population is aged 35 and below, while Africa has almost 400 million young people in the same age bracket. We want to nurture their creativity and provide mentorship by helping them develop their talents," said Professor Shaukat Abdulrazak, Kenya's Principal Secretary for the State Department for Science, Research and Innovation.
Professor Abdulrazak said the longstanding partnership between Africa and China, and between Kenya and China since independence, continues to create opportunities for cooperation in education, innovation and skills development.
Nanjing Agricultural University Vice President, Professor Feng Shuyi said the competition pushes students beyond academic theory by requiring them to develop practical solutions to societal challenges.
"The competition encourages university students to apply what they have learned in the classroom to real-world problems," Feng said.
Professor Feng Shuyi, Vice President of Nanjing Agricultural University, during the China International College Students' Innovation Competition in Nairobi, Kenya, July 28, 2026. 
 Africa
Many of the projects presented focused on improving food security, tackling water shortages, preventing crop diseases and advancing healthcare technologies.
Professor Abdulrazak said that the competition gives students an opportunity to use innovation and technology to solve problems affecting communities.
"I was very impressed to see some of the projects related to health, including traditional Chinese medicine that is being implemented by the African younger generation. We also saw areas of biotechnology aimed at enhancing food safety and food security," Prof. Abdulrazak said.
Professor Shaukat Abdulrazak, Kenya's Principal Secretary for the State Department for Science, Research and Innovation, during the China International College Students' Innovation Competition in Nairobi, Kenya, July 28, 2026. 
 Africa
Among the gold medal-winning projects was one from Malawi's Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources, which showcased an innovation designed to improve agricultural productivity for smallholder farmers. Ufulu Kampinga, a student at the university, said the project, titled Malawi Youth Hope Seeds in Africa Science and Technology Backyard Entrepreneurship Project, aims to improve farmers' incomes, nutrition and crop production.
"Our project is helping smallholder farmers in Malawi earn more, eat enough and eat better," Kampinga said. "We encourage practices such as intercropping maize with soybeans to improve nutrition while increasing harvests so farmers can strengthen their food security throughout the year."
Fellow student Monica Didas said the team developed the project to address persistent farming challenges.
"Using this technology and the model introduced through China's support, we have been able to overcome some of those challenges," Didas said.
The competition also highlighted collaboration in healthcare and traditional medicine.
Hu Zijing, an associate professor at the University of Johannesburg who teaches traditional Chinese medicine, said the initiative strengthens exchanges between African and Chinese students.
"This platform enhances mutual understanding and collaboration between young people from Africa and China," Hu said. "It enables students to showcase their work, better understand one another and develop an international outlook."
He added that the goal extends beyond introducing traditional Chinese medicine in Africa.
"We want to integrate Chinese medicine with African traditional medicine because Africa also has a very long history of traditional medicine," he said.
University of Johannesburg student Rabone Monama demonstrated a traditional Chinese medicine rehabilitation model used to help patients with arthritis, dysmenorrhea and other pain-related conditions.
Monama said studying traditional Chinese medicine had taught her that healthcare extends beyond medication.
"We learn from nature how we live, how we eat and how we manage our emotions," she said. "The food we eat is also medicine. We can learn to take care of ourselves through healthy lifestyles before medical intervention becomes necessary."
Elina Hlatshwayo, a student at Johannesburg University where she's studying traditional Chinese medicine, during the China International College Students' Innovation Competition in Nairobi, Kenya, July 28, 2026. 
 Africa
Fellow student Elina Hlatshwayo said participating in the competition helped her develop skills beyond her academic training.
"Our course is heavily focused on clinical studies and traditional Chinese medicine, so this project allowed me to explore the technical aspects, including physics and chemistry," Hlatshwayo said.
Other participating institutions included Kenya's Egerton University and Kabarak University, alongside Uganda's Makerere University.
Organizers say the competition continues to provide a platform for African and Chinese university students to collaborate, exchange ideas and develop innovations capable of addressing shared development challenges while preparing the next generation of innovators and entrepreneurs.

articles.title: From trade to value chains: China, ASEAN deepen industrial cooperation
articles.titleCn: 从贸易到价值链：中国与东盟深化产业合作
articles.summary: As economic ties continue to deepen, Chinese companies are expanding their presence in ASEAN countries beyond exports to include investment, local production, technological cooperation and regional operations.
articles.summaryCn: 中国与东盟通过互补性合作深化产业价值链，马来西亚等国的案例展示了投资与技术转移如何促进区域协同发展。

paragraphs.en: As economic ties continue to {{0}}, Chinese companies are expanding their {{1}} in ASEAN countries beyond exports, moving into investment, local production, technological cooperation and regional operations. China and ASEAN have been each other's largest trading partners for several consecutive years. In the first half of 2026, bilateral trade reached 4.34 trillion yuan (about $643.44 billion), an increase of 18.2% year on year. However, ASEAN is far from a {{2}} market, with member states differing in development priorities, industrial strengths and policy approaches. For Chinese companies expanding across the region, the key question is how to {{3}} these differences and turn them into opportunities for more effective regional cooperation.
paragraphs.cn: 随着经济联系的持续加深，中国企业正在东盟国家扩大存在，从单纯出口转向投资、本地生产、技术合作和区域运营。中国和东盟已连续多年互为最大贸易伙伴。2026年上半年，双边贸易额达到4.34万亿元人民币（约6434.4亿美元），同比增长18.2%。然而，东盟远非一个同质化市场，各成员国在发展优先事项、产业优势和政策方针上存在差异。对于在区域内扩张的中国企业而言，关键问题是如何驾驭这些差异，并将其转化为更有效区域合作的机会。

paragraphs.en: In a recent interview with Bridging News, Kat W. Wong, executive director at the Center for Advanced Studies and Research Malaysia, proposed the concept of "ASEAN Synergy." She said ASEAN countries share many similarities, but each has its own priorities. If they compete for the same industries, investments and projects, competition within the region is inevitable. A more effective approach, she said, is to identify {{4}} roles across countries. Two or three countries, for example, could {{5}} in the same industry, each contributing to different parts of the value chain and sharing resources and processes.

As economic ties continue to deepen, Chinese companies are expanding their presence in ASEAN countries beyond exports, moving into investment, local production, technological cooperation and regional operations.
China and ASEAN have been each other's largest trading partners for several consecutive years. In the first half of 2026, bilateral trade reached 4.34 trillion yuan (about $643.44 billion), an increase of 18.2% year on year.
However, ASEAN is far from a homogeneous market, with member states differing in development priorities, industrial strengths and policy approaches. For Chinese companies expanding across the region, the key question is how to navigate these differences and turn them into opportunities for more effective regional cooperation.
In a recent interview with Bridging News, Kat W. Wong, executive director at the Center for Advanced Studies and Research Malaysia, proposed the concept of "ASEAN Synergy." She said ASEAN countries share many similarities, but each has its own priorities. If they compete for the same industries, investments and projects, competition within the region is inevitable.
A more effective approach, she said, is to identify complementary roles across countries. Two or three countries, for example, could collaborate in the same industry, each contributing to different parts of the value chain and sharing resources and processes.
Cross-border energy cooperation offers one example. Laos provides electricity, Thailand and Malaysia connect regional power grids, and Singapore provides market demand. Each country plays a different role based on its own strengths. In January 2026, power authorities from Laos, Thailand and Malaysia signed a second-phase transmission agreement to further advance the four-country power trading arrangement.
For Chinese companies, investing in one ASEAN country does not have to mean operating in a single market. It can also provide access to resources, production and markets across the region, allowing companies to participate more deeply in ASEAN value chains.
Malaysia offers a case in point. Huang said the country's multilingual, multiethnic society and open market are among its key attractions for international investors. But Malaysia is looking for more than capital and projects. Foreign investment, she said, should also bring technology, expertise and spillover benefits to local industries.
The numbers underline the importance of foreign investment. In 2025, Malaysia approved 207.1 billion Malaysian ringgits ($50.65 billion) in foreign investment, accounting for 48.5% of total investment. China was the country's second-largest source of foreign investment.
Proton, the Malaysian carmaker backed by China's Geely Automobile Holdings Ltd., launched its electric vehicle production plant, marking the country's first foray into EV manufacturing, Perak, Malaysia, September 4, 2025. 
The partnership between China's Geely and Malaysian automaker Proton shows how foreign investment can support the local economy. Since Geely acquired a stake in Proton, the companies have cooperated on vehicle and technology development, intellectual property, local parts production and supplier participation. The partnership raised local content in some Proton models to 82%, Malaysian Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani told local media outlet The Star.
Huang said China's advances in areas such as artificial intelligence could also benefit Malaysia. AI is already being used in demand forecasting, production planning, order management and logistics, helping businesses improve efficiency. But she stressed that cooperation should go beyond technology transfer. Malaysia ultimately needs to build its own technological and innovation capabilities.
She sees further opportunities for China and Malaysia to cooperate in AI, local innovation and talent development. Technical and vocational education and training, or TVET, could play an important role by promoting knowledge exchange, skills training and greater participation of local talent in industrial development.
This shift from market entry to joint technology and capacity building is gaining momentum in China-Malaysia cooperation, and China's southwestern Chongqing Municipality can offer a vivid example.
Chongqing-based Zonsen, a major Chinese industrial manufacturing company, has strengthened market and industrial cooperation with Malaysian partners, while the Harbin Institute of Technology's Chongqing Research Institute has worked with Malaysian universities in areas including AI and intelligent manufacturing.
Huang said Chongqing has strong capabilities in efficient, large-scale manufacturing, while Malaysia seeks to add more value to products and services and is well positioned to connect with markets across Southeast Asia. Their complementarity therefore goes beyond a simple model of "made in Chongqing, sold in Malaysia." It could extend across manufacturing, technology, talent, services and regional markets.

articles.fullText:
Google's head of AI, Demis Hassabis, will step down from his current role to become Alphabet's chief scientist amid a reshuffling at DeepMind that will also include a key engineer's departure.
Hassabis will take on two new titles, Alphabet announced on Wednesday: chair of DeepMind and chief scientist of Alphabet.
The change "will allow me to focus on long-term strategy, and accelerating scientific breakthroughs, including leaning into my work at Isomorphic to help cure disease," Hassabis wrote in a social media post.
Isomorphic Labs is an AI-powered drug discovery lab that spun out from DeepMind in 2021. In 2024, Hassabis won a Nobel Prize in chemistry.
As part of the shake up, DeepMind's chief technology officer and chief AI architect Koray Kavukcuoglu will become the division's senior vice president and oversee its operations, including the development of Google's flagship frontier models and products which are known as Gemini.
Longtime Google engineer Jeff Dean is also leaving the company after nearly three decades to "try something new, and we're excited to support him in that," Google CEO Sundar Pichai said in a blog post announcing the news.
Hassabis co-founded DeepMind in 2010, and four years later, Google bought the research lab for $650 million, according to reports at the time. His co-founder, Mustafa Suleyman, is currently the chief of Microsoft's AI segment.
Google is competing for customers alongside other major AI developers including Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, as well as DeepSeek and Moonshot in China.
The industry is also chasing a theoretical milestone known as advanced general intelligence (AGI), which is a point when AI software matches the capabilities of human thinking.
"I've been working towards AGI my whole life and now, like many of you, I feel it is close at hand," Hassabis wrote in Wednesday's blog post.
"With this backdrop, I've decided that now is the right time for me to hand over my day-to-day operational responsibilities at (Google DeepMind), so that I have the time and space to focus on the big picture and help influence what is to come," Hassabis continued.
Observers have been waiting for Google to announce a more powerful version of its AI model, called Gemini 3.5 Pro, which was supposed to launch in June but appears to be delayed.
Its shares closed 4% down Wednesday afternoon.
The leadership changes come amid a wider brain drain at Google.
In June, a top AI and engineering executive, Noam Shazeer, left for OpenAI, while senior researcher John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in chemistry with Hassabis, jumped to Anthropic.
articles.fullTextCn:
谷歌AI负责人德米斯·哈萨比斯将卸任当前职务，成为Alphabet的首席科学家，与此同时DeepMind进行重组，包括一名关键工程师的离职。Alphabet于周三宣布，哈萨比斯将担任两个新职务：DeepMind主席和Alphabet首席科学家。哈萨比斯在社交媒体帖子中写道，这一变动“将使我能够专注于长期战略，加速科学突破，包括深入我在Isomorphic的工作以帮助治愈疾病。”Isomorphic Labs是一家AI驱动的药物发现实验室，于2021年从DeepMind分拆出来。2024年，哈萨比斯获得了诺贝尔化学奖。

作为重组的一部分，DeepMind的首席技术官兼首席AI架构师科拉伊·卡武克丘奥卢将成为该部门的高级副总裁，负责其运营，包括开发谷歌旗舰前沿模型和产品，即Gemini。长期在谷歌工作的工程师杰夫·迪恩在近三十年后也将离开公司，以“尝试新事物，我们很高兴支持他这样做，”谷歌CEO桑达尔·皮查伊在宣布此消息的博客文章中表示。哈萨比斯于2010年共同创立了DeepMind，四年后，据当时报道，谷歌以6.5亿美元收购了该研究实验室。他的联合创始人穆斯塔法·苏莱曼目前是微软AI部门的主管。谷歌正与其他主要AI开发者竞争客户，包括微软、OpenAI、Anthropic和Meta，以及中国的DeepSeek和Moonshot。

该行业还在追逐一个理论里程碑，称为高级通用智能（AGI），即AI软件达到人类思维能力水平的时刻。“我一生都在致力于AGI，现在，像你们许多人一样，我觉得它近在咫尺，”哈萨比斯在周三的博客文章中写道。“在这种背景下，我决定现在是时候将我在（谷歌DeepMind）的日常运营职责交接出去，以便我有时间和空间专注于大局，并帮助影响未来，”哈萨比斯继续说道。观察者一直在等待谷歌宣布其AI模型的更强大版本，称为Gemini 3.5 Pro，该模型原定于6月推出，但似乎被推迟。其股价周三下午收盘下跌4%。

领导层变动发生在谷歌更广泛的人才流失背景下。6月，顶级AI和工程高管诺姆·沙泽尔离职加入OpenAI，而高级研究员约翰·詹珀，与哈萨比斯共同获得2024年诺贝尔化学奖，跳槽到Anthropic。

articles.fullText:
The first integrated AI platform for early pine wilt disease was introduced in China's eastern city of Nanjing on August 12.
Pine wilt disease, often referred to as the "cancer of pine trees," rarely causes visible discoloration during the early stages of infection. This makes timely detection difficult through manual inspections or conventional images alone. By the time obvious changes become visible in a tree's crown, the disease may already have progressed to the middle or late stages.
Pine wilt disease is difficult to detect in its early stages. Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China, August 12, 2026./Nanjing Forestry University
The AI platform was co-generated by Nanjing Forestry University and China's internet giant Baidu.
In traditional research workflows, researchers draw on forestry expertise to identify potentially effective features across a wide range of spectral bands, vegetation indices and their combinations, then validate them individually through extensive experiments. Validating every combination manually is not only time-consuming but can also introduce bias based on researchers' prior experience.
Working with Baidu's Famou AI agent, the team uses an AI platform to automatically generate, test and compare different feature combinations, allowing researchers to quickly identify the most promising solutions for further experimentation.
A researcher analyzes the data of the pine trees in Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China, August 12, 2026./Nanjing Forestry University
At present, Nanjing Forestry University's pine wilt disease detection and prevention technology has been deployed across Jiangsu, Liaoning, Anhui and other provinces, covering approximately 133,333 hectares in total, an area 1.82 times the size of Singapore.
The AI solutions are expected to further strengthen early-warning capabilities across around 3,333 to 66,667 hectares of high-risk pine forests. They are also projected to reduce the costs of verification, prevention and control operations, and model iteration by around 30 million to 50 million yuan, or US$4.42 million to US$7.37 million.

articles.fullText:
In late July, US officials accused China's Moonshot of "industrial-scale distillation" of Anthropic's AI and threatened sanctions.
So what exactly is "distillation"? Does it amount to copying? And how did China's AI models achieve their rapid breakthroughs?
Distillation is standard practice, widely used by US tech giants like Google and xAI.
Calling it "theft" is seen by many as a commercial tactic to slow down competitors, not a technical reality.
US officials charge that large-scale unauthorized distillation violates terms of service and raises national security concerns.
China's Commerce Ministry has hit back, accusing Washington of "double standards" and "typical AI hegemony." It pointed out that many US AI companies have distilled Chinese models in their own R&D, using the very technique the administration is now trying to ban.
Elon Musk's team used it for Grok. Google even sells a distillation service. And Jensen Huang, Nvidia's CEO, put it best: "Distillation, learning from AI, learning from other sources of knowledge, is fundamental to intelligence."
That's not theft – that's how intelligence works.
The key point is this: distillation alone cannot produce a model with the performance of Kimi K3. Moonshot says the leap came from its own architecture, a new optimizer called Moon Clip, a linear-attention system and attention residuals – breakthroughs Musk once praised. Original engineering, not a copy, at about a third of Anthropic's flagship price per task.
And here's a telling contrast: on OpenRouter, US companies now run nearly 60% of their tokens on Chinese models. In July, Hugging Face – an American platform – had to call in a Chinese model to fight off an attack that US frontier models couldn't handle. Washington wants to cut off what Silicon Valley is already buying.
Distillation was never the whole story. It's about who gets to define innovation. And China's advancements have made that conversation truly global.
articles.fullTextCn:
七月下旬，美国官员指责中国的月之暗面公司对Anthropic的AI进行“工业规模蒸馏”，并威胁实施制裁。那么，“蒸馏”到底是什么？这算抄袭吗？中国AI模型又是如何实现快速突破的？蒸馏是标准做法，被谷歌和xAI等美国科技巨头广泛使用。

许多人认为，称其为“盗窃”是一种商业策略，旨在减缓竞争对手的速度，而非技术现实。美国官员指控，未经授权的大规模蒸馏违反了服务条款，并引发国家安全担忧。中国商务部反击，指责华盛顿“双重标准”和“典型的AI霸权”。商务部指出，许多美国AI公司在自己的研发中蒸馏了中国模型，使用了美国政府现在试图禁止的技术。埃隆·马斯克的团队在Grok中使用了该技术。谷歌甚至出售蒸馏服务。

英伟达CEO黄仁勋说得最好：“蒸馏，从AI中学习，从其他知识来源中学习，是智能的基础。”这不是盗窃——这就是智能的运作方式。关键在于：仅靠蒸馏无法产生具有Kimi K3性能的模型。月之暗面表示，这一飞跃来自其自身架构、名为Moon Clip的新优化器、线性注意力系统和注意力残差——这些是马斯克曾称赞的突破。这是原创工程，而非复制，且每任务成本约为Anthropic旗舰产品的三分之一。一个鲜明的对比是：在OpenRouter上，美国公司现在近60%的令牌运行在中国模型上。

七月，美国平台Hugging Face不得不调用中国模型来抵御美国前沿模型无法处理的攻击。华盛顿想切断硅谷已经在购买的东西。蒸馏从来不是全部。关键在于谁有资格定义创新。而中国的进步使这场对话真正全球化。
